Retrieved via Exa search highlights. Both approved domains (cnn.com, independent.co.uk).

- A powerful earthquake struck Mexico's southern Pacific coast on Friday 17 July 2026, near the Guatemalan border, felt from Mexico City to El Salvador.
- USGS preliminary magnitude 7.3 (some outlets/Mexican civil protection reported 7.4). Epicentre ~48 km (30 miles) southwest of Aquiles Serdan, off the coast of Chiapas; depth ~15 km (9 miles). Quake struck ~08:48 local time.
- Preceded by a smaller tremor further out to sea; followed by at least 10 aftershocks ranging magnitude 4.9 to 6 (one ~5.2).
- Pacific Tsunami Warning Center issued then LIFTED a tsunami advisory (waves 30cm-1m possible within 300km); Guatemala observed sub-1-metre tsunamis; threat later declared passed. Navy advised staying away from beaches for six hours.
- No deaths reported in any country. Two to four people injured in southern Mexico (reports vary). No severe/major damage; some minor structural damage and landslides on roads.
- Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum: said on X she had spoken with the governors of Chiapas and Tabasco and that, so far, no damage had been reported in either state; preliminary reports showed no damage.
- Guatemala's President Bernardo Arevalo: quake caused landslides in San Pedro La Laguna but no major incidents (per UPI).
- Guatemala's CONRED reported no immediate damage. El Salvador felt strong shaking, evacuations, no deaths/damage.
- Region is quake-prone; a 7.1 quake in 2017 killed hundreds in Mexico City. Mexico City alert did NOT sound this time (energy in first seconds did not exceed activation thresholds, govt said).
